title: Fasting Obligations in Ramadan
summary: Fulfilling Ramadan fasts is a sacred obligation and must be compensated if missed.
translation: If during the blessed month of Ramadan, something happens unexpectedly causing one to miss a fast, there should be no negligence in this matter. For instance, if someone falls ill during Ramadan and is unable to fast, they should make up for it later when they can. Because if a person does not fast, the obligation will remain on them, and they will be questioned about it on the Day of Judgment. Therefore, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said that if a person passes away with obligatory Ramadan fasts pending, each missed fast should be compensated by feeding one needy person. This is why scholars state that the compensation for one fast is equivalent to one 'sadaqat al-fitr,' ensuring the needs of one needy person are met. Those who can fast themselves are required to do so; otherwise, they will be sinful and evading duties despite being able-bodied is also sinful. One should pray to Allah Almighty and seek strength to fulfill the acts of worship.
